glossario.simples: The Chamber of Deputies and the Federal Senate together: it is where the country's laws are made.
Having two lawmaking Houses, like the National Congress.
The House that checks and reviews a bill that the other House has already approved. In Portuguese: Casa revisora.
The time an elected person stays in office. In Portuguese: mandato.
Smaller groups of lawmakers that study the bills on one subject.
Comissão de Constituição e Justiça (Constitution and Justice Committee): it checks whether a bill respects the Constitution.
The meeting with all the members of the House, where the big votes happen. In Portuguese: Plenário.
The list of what will be discussed and voted on. In Portuguese: pauta.
To follow and check whether someone is doing the job right and following the rules.
The plan for how much money the government will receive and how it will spend it during the year.
Comissão Parlamentar de Inquérito (Parliamentary Inquiry Committee): a group of lawmakers that investigates a fact.
A process that can remove a president from office, for example for breaking serious rules of the Constitution.
A group of lawmakers from the same party, from the same state or with the same interest. In Portuguese: bancada.
A group of lawmakers from several parties who get together to debate a topic. In Portuguese: frente parlamentar.
The parties and lawmakers who support the government. In Portuguese: base do governo.
The parties and lawmakers who oppose the government.
A lawmaker chosen to speak for their group and to guide how the group votes.
People who hold a term of office in a lawmaking House: deputies, senators and city councilors. In Portuguese: parlamentares.
The official meetings of a lawmaking House.
The most important law of the country. All other laws must respect it.
Supremo Tribunal Federal (Supreme Federal Court): the highest court in the country, which takes care of the Constitution.
People who take care of areas of the government (or, in the case of the STF, the judges of the court).
The House where the state deputies make the state's laws. In Portuguese: Assembleia Legislativa.
The lawmaking House of the Federal District, where the district deputies work. In Portuguese: Câmara Legislativa.
The House where the city councilors make the city's laws. In Portuguese: Câmara Municipal.
Cities, with their rural areas. Each one has a mayor and city councilors.

slides.texto: It is where the country's laws are made. It is in Brasília, the capital, and has two Houses: the Chamber of Deputies (Câmara dos Deputados) and the Federal Senate (Senado Federal).

slides.titulo: Two Houses, two ways of representing
slides.texto: The Chamber of Deputies and the Federal Senate together form the National Congress.

itens: States with more people have more deputies: at least 8, at most 70.
4-year term of office. All the seats are chosen in the same election.
colunas.exemplo: São Paulo, the state with the most people, has 70 deputies. Acre, Roraima and the DF have 8 each.

itens: It represents the **states** and the DF.
It has 81 senators: 3 per state and 3 for the DF.
Big state or small state: they all have the same number.
8-year term of office. Every 4 years, 1/3 or 2/3 of the seats change.
colunas.exemplo: In 2026, each state chose 2 senators. In the next election, each state chooses 1.

slides.titulo: Imagine the school creating a rule...

quadros.txt: The school is going to create a new rule for recess.
First, the class representatives vote. Bigger classes have more representatives.
Then, a council with 3 students from each grade checks the rule. Every grade has the same weight.
If the council changes something, the rule goes back to the representatives, who have the final word.

slides.moral: Congress works like this: the Chamber speaks for the people, and the Senate for the states. One House reviews the other: this is the **bicameral** system.

slides.texto: Before the vote with everyone, bills go through smaller groups: the **committees**.

itens.txt: Each committee takes care of one subject: health, education, sports, the environment...
The Chamber has 30 permanent committees. The Senate has 16.
The CCJ (Constitution and Justice Committee) checks whether the bill respects the Constitution.
The **Plenary** (Plenário) is the meeting with everyone in the House. That is where the big votes happen.
Many bills are decided only in the committees, without going to the Plenary.

slides.coruja: In the Chamber, the full name of the CCJ is Comissão de Constituição e Justiça e de Cidadania (CCJC): Constitution, Justice and Citizenship Committee.

slides.texto: The president is chosen by their own colleagues, for a term of office of **2 years**.

itens.txt: The deputies elect the president of the Chamber. The senators elect the president of the Senate.
The president sets the **agenda**: the list of what will be voted on in the Plenary.
They open and lead the sessions and organize the work of the House.
The president of the Senate also presides over Congress when the two Houses meet together.

slides.coruja: If the President and the Vice President of the Republic are not available, the president of the Chamber takes over for a while. Next in line are the president of the Senate and the president of the STF.

slides.titulo: Congress does more than make laws
slides.texto: See other tasks of deputies and senators:

itens.txt: **Oversee** the government. Congress can even call ministers to give explanations.
Approve the **budget**, which says how the country's money can be spent.
Create a CPI (Parliamentary Inquiry Committee), a committee that investigates a fact. It only takes 1/3 of the members of the House asking for it.
Approve some of the president's choices, like the STF ministers. This is done by the Senate.
Handle impeachment: the Chamber authorizes the process and the Senate holds the trial.

slides.coruja: Stop 8 has a full explanation of CPIs and impeachment.

slides.texto: States, the DF and municipalities also have a lawmaking House. But there, it is just one House.

cards.txt: Makes the laws of the Federal District.
cards.mais: The DF cannot be divided into municipalities. That is why the Legislative Chamber makes laws that, in a state, would be made by the Legislative Assembly and by the City Councils.

dados.val: City councilors: the number depends on the population

slides.texto: Inside Congress, lawmakers organize themselves into groups.

itens.txt: **Caucus**: a group from the same party, from the same state or with the same interest.
**Parliamentary front**: people from several parties who get together to debate a topic.
Government's base: the parties and lawmakers who support the government.
Opposition: the parties and lawmakers who oppose the government.
Parties and blocs have a leader in the House. The President of the Republic names the government's leader.

slides.coruja: The base and the opposition change over time: they depend on who is governing.

slides.pergunta: How many senators does each state have?
slides.explica: Every state and the DF have 3 senators, whether they are big or small. In the Chamber it is different: it depends on the population.

slides.pergunta: The Chamber passed a bill that started there. What happens now?
opcoes: The STF votes on the bill
slides.explica: The Senate is the reviewing House: it checks the bill. Only after that does the bill go to the President of the Republic.
